It answers "where in the sequence" (name → email → email_verify → dob), which is why email_verify holds at step 2 rather than having a segment of its own. Do not put a screen name in it: a screen and a step are different things. Screen identity lives in §11 (screen_id + screen_name), and both travel on their own events. A row with step_index "—" (notifications, reachability, phonebook, location) is outside every progress bar and is NOT a step for funnel purposes: profile_step_viewed requires an int step_index, so it does not fire for them. Those ids exist so that profile_step_skipped — which carries step_id + screen_id and no index — has a stable value when the screen has a skip. Added 21 Sep 2026 with the Profile 09 ticket.

naming_rules: screen_name: "<Flow> - <Screen>", the flow prefix taken from the epic and the screen in the words the ticket uses. Readable at a glance in a long analytics dropdown, and it sorts by flow.
screen_id: snake_case of the same words, prefixed by flow. Assigned once. If a screen is renamed, the label changes and the id does not.
One row per screen, not per state. A screen with ten states is one screen_id carrying a state property (see ConnectSSO).
A screen with no row has no ticket. If the row is missing, add it here first — that is the step that stops an event name being invented.

The two embrace bridges are TWO screens, not two states of one — they sit at different points in the flow and carry different copy. They share a shell and a variant value set (§16); they do not share a screen_id. Added 9 Sep 2026, before the Profile 05 ticket was written.

A bridge screen is a screen but NOT a step. profile_embrace_build has a row here and deliberately has no row in §2 — firing profile_step_viewed on it would put a phantom step in the completion funnel.

ProfilePhotos is step 1 of a DIFFERENT group ("The real you"), not a fifth step of "The basics". Its step_index is 1 within that group; §2 also records that photos sits outside the Share-some-details progress bar. Two progress bars, two vocabularies — do not renumber one against the other.

The photos screen's PERMISSION states have no events yet. A card-shown / mode / granted / refused / returned-from-settings set must be defined in events.json (with a closed access_status value set here) BEFORE the Profile 06 sprint — flagged 9 Sep 2026. Until then the screen's most likely drop-off point is invisible.

Profile 06 requests NO library permission (system picker on iOS and Android 13+), so the library access card is Android ≤ 12 only and there is no limited-access state at all. Any access_status value set defined later must cover the CAMERA (both platforms, always) and the old-Android library case — not an iOS library status, which we never read.

sets.name: media_prompt_id registry
sets.note: THE MEDIA PROMPT DICTIONARY. Separate from prompt_topic_id (§17) and topic_id (§6) — those are the written prompts on the profile; these are the eleven things a person can say in ten or fifteen seconds. STORE AND SEND THE ID, NEVER THE DISPLAY STRING: the prompts are copy, they will be edited, and an edit must not orphan the clips recorded under them. Position is the order the list renders and is fixed; own_idea is always last and always carries is_own_prompt: true. The SAME eleven are offered for video and for voice — nothing in the id says which, so type is required on every event that carries one. preview_on marks the prompt shown on an empty card, per medium, which is the one the user sees before opening the list. Position stays fixed — the LIST order does not move, only the preview does; a list that reorders itself makes a user who came back for row 7 hunt for it.

sets.name: sheet dismiss_method
sets.note: THE CANONICAL SHEET-CLOSE VOCABULARY, and the only one: every bottom sheet in the product reports its dismissal with these four values. Carried by prompt_editor_dismissed, prompt_topic_list_dismissed and media_prompt_list_dismissed, and by every sheet added after them. close is the X or a Cancel control; backdrop is a tap on the scrim; swipe is the drag-down gesture; system_back is the Android gesture or hardware key, which is NOT the same act as the X and must not be folded into it (decision 32). Created 16 Sep 2026 by unifying three drifted spellings of the same four acts — close|scrim|swipe|back on the prompts write sheet and cancel|backdrop|swipe|system_back on the media prompt list. Neither had shipped, so nothing in the warehouse needed migrating; a sheet-close value outside this set is a bug at the call site. Never use the key method for this (§8): method already means phone · apple · google. Also carried by search_coach_dismissed (Search 01 actions coach, 21 Oct 2026): close = Got it or Don't show again (told apart by dont_show_again), backdrop = the scrim, system_back = Android back; swipe never occurs there. Values unchanged.

sets.name: permission_status
sets.note: THE OS PERMISSION STATE, for every permission in §8's type set. Four values, one vocabulary across both platforms: not_determined (never asked — the only state in which our own sheet can be raised), granted, denied (includes 'permanently denied' — the distinction is the platform's rationale flag, which is a BEHAVIOUR branch, not a second value), restricted (parental controls / MDM; treated as denied everywhere in the product). Carried by permission_status_changed as from and to. NOT a consent: consent is §8 channel and lives on our server, this is the device's answer and is re-read on every foreground rather than remembered. limited is deliberately absent — it is a photo-library concept and stays on permission_result's own type. Android <= 12 notifications have no runtime permission at all and are reported as granted. Created 21 Sep 2026 with the Profile 09 ticket.

sets.name: interest_channel
sets.note: THE DEMAND TEST on Stay reachable (Profile 10), MVP only. A checked box records interest in a channel that does NOT exist yet — it is not a consent, nothing is sent on it, and no contact data is collected for it. Deliberately a separate vocabulary from §8 channel so an interest can never be read as a consent. ai_call is the phone call from our AI assistant (§8 call when it ships). Created 25 Sep 2026 with the Profile 10 ticket.

sets.name: location_unavailable_reason
sets.note: WHY LOCATION IS UNAVAILABLE, one set for every surface that blocks on it. not_determined: never asked (the only reason our ask can raise the OS dialog). denied: the OS permission is denied or restricted (§24 — restricted is treated as denied). services_off: the device-wide Location switch is off, so no app can get location and the OS dialog will not appear; it is NOT a §24 permission status, which is why it needs this set. Profile 12 sends denied · services_off on permission_denied_recovery_shown; the app-wide gate sends all three on location_gate_shown. Created 5 Oct 2026 with the Profile 12 ticket.

sets.name: check_in_gate_target
sets.note: WHAT REOPENED THE CHECK-IN from checkin_search_unavailable. cta: the screen's "Check-in for a date" button. search_tab / instant_tab: the bottom tabs — both lead to the Check-In, because a search needs stated availability first. Settings is not a value: it does not reopen anything. Created 12 Oct 2026 with the Check-In 01 ticket.

sets.name: check_in_step
sets.note: THE 48hrs CHECK-IN SCREENS, in flow order. intro is a bridge (no StepProgress) but IS a value here, because check_in_closed can fire on it; check_in_step_answered never carries intro. Kit: ScreenCheckIn steps 1–7. prep removed 13 Oct 2026 (registry 1.4.20) with the heads-up time step. Created 12 Oct 2026 with the Check-In 01 ticket; each step ticket confirms its own value. today and tomorrow confirmed by Check-In 02, 13 Oct 2026 (registry 1.4.21). motivation confirmed by Check-In 03, 13 Oct 2026 (registry 1.4.22). vibe confirmed by Check-In 04, 13 Oct 2026 (registry 1.4.23). filters confirmed by Check-In 05, 13 Oct 2026 (registry 1.4.24). uplift CONFIRMED by Check-In 06 (13 Oct 2026): the last step; check_in_step_answered on uplift fires once, on a SUCCESSFUL commit.

sets.name: check_in_no_hours_today_action
sets.note: HOW THE “No hours today?” CONFIRM WAS ANSWERED, on checkin_today with an empty grid. continue_tomorrow: the sunset “Continue to tomorrow” button — the user goes on with no hours today. pick_today: “Cancel, pick hours today”. dismissed: scrim tap or Android back — the same outcome as pick_today (stays on Today) but not the same act, so it is kept apart. Created 13 Oct 2026 with the Check-In 02 ticket.

sets.name: check_in_motivation
sets.note: THE ONE MOTIVATION A USER STATES FOR A CHECK-IN, on checkin_motivation (Check-In 03). SINGLE-SELECT: exactly one value per accepted Continue, never a list. In the kit's list order. Kit: CHECKIN_MOTIVATIONS in screens-checkin.jsx; Instant's INSTANT_MOTIVES uses the same ids. The same vocabulary is the dating_intent filter (§10) — no mapping table. Class 1: non_monogamy discloses a relationship practice. Shown on the profile (one MotivationPill) only while a Check-In is active. Created 13 Oct 2026 with the Check-In 03 ticket.

sets.name: check_in_vibe
sets.note: THE VIBES A USER STATES FOR A CHECK-IN, on checkin_vibe (Check-In 04). MULTI-SELECT: 1–5 values per accepted Continue, across all three groups. In the kit's list order (CHECKIN_VIBE_GROUPS in screens-checkin.jsx); a list of picks is always sent in this order, never in tap order. The group is a property of the value, not a second id — never send it separately. Class 0: none of the values discloses a special category. ONE vocabulary: Search's “vibe today” card and Instant show these labels (CHECKIN_VIBE_LABEL) and no others. Shown on the profile only while a Check-In is active. Created 13 Oct 2026 with the Check-In 04 ticket.

sets.name: check_in_commit_failure
sets.note: WHY A CHECK-IN COMMIT (Find my date on checkin_uplift, Check-In 06) DID NOT SAVE. network = no response / timeout · server = any 5xx or unexpected error · contact_info = the server rejected the uplift text for an email, phone number or link the client detector let through (the client then shows the contact-info state, not the save-failed card). Closed set; one value per check_in_commit_failed. Created 13 Oct 2026 with the Check-In 06 ticket.

sets.name: like_abandon_stage
sets.note: WHERE THE LIKE FLOW WAS LEFT WITHOUT SENDING (like_confirm_abandoned). confirm = Cancel or dismiss on Be sure · message = dismiss on the message sheet. Skip message sends the like and is never an abandon. Created 20 Oct 2026 with Search 01.

sets.name: search_pass_type
sets.note: WHICH PASS ON THE 1-UP PROFILE (pass_sent). not_now = hidden until the viewer’s next Check-In · not_interested = removed from the viewer’s pool for good, no undo on the 1-up profile. On a received like (Search 03), not_interested also declines the like, after a 6 s Undo. Created 20 Oct 2026 with Search 01.

sets.name: like_surface
sets.note: WHERE A LIKE OR A CONFIRM WAS STARTED (like_tapped, like_sent). profile = the Like / Confirm date button on the full profile (Freemium queue, or opened from the grid or the Likes tab — referrer_screen_id of the profile visit tells them apart) · grid_card RETIRED 21 Oct 2026, never shipped: there is no Like from a grid card, a tap anywhere on it opens the profile · likes_received = Not interested on a Likes tab card, or on a profile opened from it (the decline is sent from the Likes list's toast). Not used by like_tapped: Confirm date on a Likes card opens the profile, where the confirm is surface profile. Also the surface of pass_sent (profile · likes_received), pass_undone (profile · likes_received) and like_confirm_failed (profile) (1.4.28). Created 20 Oct 2026 with Search 02; likes_received is used by Search 03.

sets.name: like_close_reason
sets.note: WHY AN OPEN LIKE CLOSED WITHOUT A DECISION (like_withdrawn, server · like_confirm_failed, client). matched = either person's other like became mutual first (1 match = 1 date) → the receiver sees a Too late card · no_overlap = the two Check-Ins have no meet-time overlap left → the receiver sees an Out of time card. Both kept until the next visit after they were seen. Created 20 Oct 2026 with Search 03.

sets.name: nav_tab
sets.note: THE TABBAR ITEMS (tab_switched). In bar order. likes is in EVERY user's bar (Search 03; amended 21 Oct 2026 — was Premium-only), with the badge. tab_switched · likes fires for Freemium too; the upsell screen it opens is its own story. Created 20 Oct 2026 with Search 03; replaces tab_switched's old inline meet|instant|score|profile.
